A corridor of light: two planes of every colour streaming out of a burning slit, turning as they come.

aerowarptics.gate.passage.quiet.about: No tunnel and no motion. The view dims, holds, and brightens into the far side.
aerowarptics.gate.passage.timey_wimey.ab: A spiral of storm cloud, ember red sliding to cold blue, turning hard with lightning down its length.

The charge drains with every block flown, and the ship slows for terrain ahead and for land that has not loaded yet.

aerowarptics.guide.page.berth_moor.hand: A ship flown in slowly by hand is caught too. Crouch while it is drawn in to break free.
aerowarptics.guide.page.berth_moor.leave: Start the drive to cast off. Cast Off on the berth, or a redstone pulse into it, does the same.
aerowarptics.guide.page.berth_moor.refus: With no berth free, or none big enough, the launch is refused before anything moves.

aerowarptics.guide.page.berth_moor.warp: Warp to the anchor as usual. The ship gets the smallest free berth it fits, and is turned to it and held.
aerowarptics.guide.page.berth_slip.fit: A ship needs two clear blocks all round, so a slip takes a ship four blocks smaller each way.
aerowarptics.guide.page.berth_slip.panel: Click it: the camera lifts. Set the slip's size, facing and place, and keep its lane clear.
aerowarptics.guide.page.berth_slip.place: Set it down within reach of an anchor you own. Its slip starts out beyond the block.

aerowarptics.guide.page.chart.pick: Right-click the table and pick a destination.
aerowarptics.guide.page.chart.shows: It gives distance, cost, reach, and the ground you would land on.

aerowarptics.guide.page.chute.feed: Feed it like any Create machine.
aerowarptics.guide.page.chute.pair: Place two chutes and pair one with the other.
aerowarptics.guide.page.chute.title: The Rift Chute
aerowarptics.guide.page.chute.what: A chute sends items to another chute, so a moving ship need not line up with a belt.
aerowarptics.guide.page.closing.draws: It draws essence steadily, and the rift shrinks as it does.
aerowarptics.guide.page.closing.place: Stand a Spatial Siphon within a few blocks of the fissure.
aerowarptics.guide.page.closing.spent: A fissure holds more than one siphon does. Pipe the essence away as it fills.

aerowarptics.guide.page.cover.aim: A Rift Drive built into an airship opens a rift, and the whole vessel flies through it - hull, cargo and crew.

aerowarptics.guide.page.cover.title: Folding Space
aerowarptics.guide.page.cover.what: You stay on the deck for all of it.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_collapse.c: Switch on stabilisers around it, evenly spaced.
Its rings can only be found in scar ruins. Set it down, load a Rift Core and a Scar Heart, pipe in essence.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_collapse.r: Stand offerings on depots around it, turn it hard, and give it a redstone pulse.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_collapse.s: If unsteady, it flings or spits the core and hurts anyone close. Only the Scar Heart is lost.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_folding.ar: Put up to sixteen items in its arms. For a Pearlescent Warp Crystal, also put one Shulker Shell per crystal in its cup.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_folding.be: Turn it, fill its tank, and press Begin on its panel.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_folding.co: A Ship's Compass comes out unbound. Sneak and use it on a Rift Drive to bind it.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_folding.wh: As well as collapsing, the Collapse Cradle folds items for Rift Essence.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rifting.br: A powered Rift Brazier burns Rift Essence every second.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rifting.ca: A Rift Fissure is free. A lit brazier or an open gate's pane also works.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rifting.fa: Point an Encased Fan through an open rift, and put the items in its stream.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rifting.wh: Blow items through an open rift with an Encased Fan, the same way you would wash them.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rules.acts: Each drive tier asks for a different step: build, open, reach, collapse.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rules.clas: Turn on the Classic Recipes data pack in a world to use the old recipes.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rules.idea: Each new drive is made from things carried to the edge of the previous drive's reach.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_rules.ladd: A Mk I is built. A Mk II needs Opened Rift Lenses, a Mk III needs a Folded Warp Crystal, and a Singularity needs a core collapsed from a Scar Heart.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_scars.char: Open a Scar Chart to get a map to a scar nobody has charted yet.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_scars.choi: An open fissure can be used for rifting for free, forever. Seal it only when you need the Scar Heart.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_scars.hear: A fissure that has been emptied seals, and leaves a Scar Heart behind.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_scars.seal: Empty the tear with a siphon, and take the heart.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_storms.cal: Break a Stormglass to call a Rift Storm down on everyone.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_storms.gla: Fill a glass bottle with Rift Essence and leave it out in a storm to set.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_storms.rai: A Spatial Siphon under open sky collects rift rain in a storm, and more above the clouds.
aerowarptics.guide.page.craft_storms.rea: A set Stormglass shows whether a storm is coming.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_bow.bow: Right-click the drive and set the Bow.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_bow.compas: The bracketed compass direction is only a readout.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_bow.needle: Turn it until the needle on top points at the nose.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_bow.title: Which Way Is Forward
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_bow.why: A drive cannot tell which end of the hull is the front.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_fit.assemb: Assemble an airship as you always would.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_fit.mount: Mount a Rift Drive anywhere aboard it.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_fit.spin: Drive its shaft at or above the minimum RPM.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_fit.tiers: A drive only moves the ship it is built into, never one it is parked beside.
aerowarptics.guide.page.drive_fit.title: Fitting a Drive
aerowarptics.guide.page.faults.common: Usually: too slow, still charging, or no course set.
aerowarptics.guide.page.faults.order: The list follows the order the server checks. The first unticked line is the problem.
aerowarptics.guide.page.faults.role: The console is a diagnostic panel, not a control. It answers one question: why hasn't the ship moved?
aerowarptics.guide.page.faults.title: Reading the Console
aerowarptics.guide.page.fissures.hidden: Without goggles, you could walk through one unaware.
aerowarptics.guide.page.fissures.ruins: Look for a broken gate ring, a sunken vault, or a survey mast.
aerowarptics.guide.page.fissures.title: Rifts Already There
aerowarptics.guide.page.fissures.wear: Wear Rift Infused Goggles to see one at all.
aerowarptics.guide.page.fissures.what: Some rifts were never opened. They hang in old ruins, leaking essence.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_fold.fo: When every row is ready, press Fold.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_fold.lo: An escort that drifts in the countdown arrives late and off to one side.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_fold.ri: Rift: One sends the whole fleet through one large rift.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_fold.sl: On the flagship's Fleet Board, drag each escort to a slot, then Sound Stations.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_fold.so: Escorts hold their slots, charged and turning, until they match the flagship's hum.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_join.ow: If the flagship belongs to someone else, its owner must accept. Your own ships join straight away.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_join.ro: Set one ship's coupler to Flagship, and the others' to Escort.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_join.st: At each escort's coupler, pick the flagship and press Take Station.
aerowarptics.guide.page.flotilla_join.wh: A Rift Coupler fitted to a Rift Drive lets several ships fold as one.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_dial.cross: Anything that crosses the gate's plane comes out of the far gate: players, mobs, riders and land vehicles.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_dial.dial: Name the gate, then dial another in the same dimension.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_dial.pays: Only the gate that dialled pays. The far gate needs nothing but to exist.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_dial.title: Dialling Another
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_rails.far: Track comes out of the far gate. Build on from its end.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_rails.route: Pick a gate on the dial and press Set Route. Trains go there, even to another dimension.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_rails.title: Rails Through a Gate
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_rails.track: Run straight Create track into the bottom of the opening.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_ring.contro: Put a Rift Gate anywhere in the ring.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_ring.feed: Feed it a shaft and some Rift Essence.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_ring.ring: Lay a closed ring of Rift Gate Frame on end.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_ring.size: The opening is the size limit. Build a wider ring to let larger things through.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_ring.title: Building the Ring
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_trains.held: A redstone signal on the controller holds trains back.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_trains.shut: The gate shuts again once the last train is through.
aerowarptics.guide.page.gate_trains.wait: A train that reaches a shut gate waits while the gate dials for it, paying as a dial does.
aerowarptics.guide.page.journey.flown: The drive propels the ship through the rift. It comes out still moving.
aerowarptics.guide.page.journey.safe: If a warp cannot be made safely, it is refused before anything moves.
aerowarptics.guide.page.journey.stay: Stay on the deck. Anyone who falls off is put back in their seat.
aerowarptics.guide.page.journey.title: The Journey
aerowarptics.guide.page.modulator_link.f: If it runs out of essence or is removed, the rift goes back to the drive's own tier colours.
Feed it a little Rift Essence. It uses a trickle only while the drive is warping.
aerowarptics.guide.page.modulator_link.p: Place one against any face of a Rift Drive.
aerowarptics.guide.page.modulator_link.w: A Rift Modulator lets the pilot of a Rift Drive customise the rift it opens: its colour and its look.
aerowarptics.guide.page.modulator_look.b: A Display Link pointed at the Modulator reads the drive it is linked to, the same as one pointed at the drive itself.
aerowarptics.guide.page.modulator_look.c: Right-click for sixteen colours (left-click sets the core, right-click sets the rim), a button that cycles through fifteen themes (shift-click to go back), and a slider for how strong the effect is.
aerowarptics.guide.page.modulator_look.w: It changes everything about the rift: the opening, the corridor, and the exit shockwave.
aerowarptics.guide.page.more.advancement: Thirty advancements double as the progression, from a first Rift Core onwards.
aerowarptics.guide.page.more.goggles: Create's goggles show tier, state, charge and stress.
aerowarptics.guide.page.more.jei: JEI carries an information page on every item.
aerowarptics.guide.page.more.ponder: Hold [W] over any item from this mod for a Ponder scene.
aerowarptics.guide.page.more.title: Where to Read More
aerowarptics.guide.page.more.wiki: This book is the walkthrough. JEI, Ponder and the goggles give the detail.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_aim.exit: Set the exit around the target: how far out, which way it faces, how high, and how fast things leave.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_aim.pay: There is no range limit, but distance costs essence. Pipe it in as the plotter charges.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_aim.targ: Type the target's X and Z on the Target tab and press Survey. The ground there appears as a 3D model.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_aim.what: A relic machine that opens a rift beside itself and another at any target in this world.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_fire.eng: Turn it at 64 RPM or more and press Engage, or set it to fire on redstone, when a ship docks, or to hold the rift open as a lane.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_fire.ent: Open the Entry tab. The camera moves out to show where the entry rift will open.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_fire.see: The far rift opens only as something comes through.
aerowarptics.guide.page.plotter_fire.thr: Park a ship behind the entry, inside the amber outline. The dock helper lines it up and launches it through.
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_fix.essenc: Scanning spends Rift Essence, which is what a Spatial Siphon is for.
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_fix.fix: A finished scan leaves a fix: a location known only from the scan, with no anchor at the far end.
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_fix.set: Set your course to the fix at the Astrolabe table, as you would for an anchor.
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_fix.title: Warping to a Fix
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_scan.parti: The bar is the world being generated. A partial map says so.
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_scan.point: Aim the dial, set a distance and arrival height.
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_scan.scan: Press Scan ahead to bring back a survey of that ground.
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_scan.title: The Rift Probe
aerowarptics.guide.page.probe_scan.why: Anchors only reach where somebody has walked.
aerowarptics.guide.page.siphon.fluid: Essence is a real fluid. Create's pipes can move it, and gates and probes use it up.
aerowarptics.guide.page.siphon.odds: A longer jump gives a better chance of a larger catch, but nothing is guaranteed.
aerowarptics.guide.page.siphon.title: The Spatial Siphon
aerowarptics.guide.page.siphon.what: Bolt one to the hull. Each time the ship comes out of a rift, it catches some Rift Essence.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer.charge: Fill it with 4 buckets of essence and turn it fast.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer.fire: Give it a signal and stand clear. The frame unravels into a seed.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer.gutters: The tear seals in 20 minutes unless a wellhead holds it.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer.ring: Build a gate ring, 3 to 7 across, with a Sunderer in it.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer.title: Tearing One Open
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer.what: No fissure near home? Make the ruin yourself.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer_risks.c: Stand out of the opening. Loose things are swallowed.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer_risks.l: The far side is not always empty.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer_risks.m: Stopped early, it misfires and hands half the essence back.
aerowarptics.guide.page.sunderer_risks.r: Stopped late, or the ring broken, and it ruptures: a crater.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_field.charg: It banks a charge and the field runs on that, loaded or not. A wider field costs more.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_field.feed: Run a shaft into the middle of any side, or up under its middle, at 32 RPM or more, and pipe in Rift Essence.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_field.place: Set it down on the ground with three clear blocks each way. It cannot be moved or carried.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_field.title: Holding a Field
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_field.what: A relic machine that holds a field over the ground round it and turns rifts aside.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_hold.panel: Click it: the camera lifts to show the field. Set its radius and switch it on.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_hold.throug: On the Who tab choose whom it turns: everyone, all but some networks, or only some.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_hold.title: What It Turns
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_hold.turned: Whoever it turns comes out at the field's edge instead, by ship or by plotted rift.
aerowarptics.guide.page.ward_hold.worn: Each rift turned costs charge. A Rift Storm thins the field. Better drives push further in.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wellhead.collar: Set a Rift Collar in one side, with a crystal in it.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wellhead.frame: Build a cube round it: Rift Casing edges, Warp Glass faces.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wellhead.title: The Wellhead
aerowarptics.guide.page.wellhead.trade: Three, five or seven blocks. A held fissure rifts nothing.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wellhead.what: A fissure can be farmed instead of drained. It takes a frame.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wellhead_running: Feed blocks in at the top. Pipe essence out of any other face.
More strain digests faster. Too much, and it runs away.
A pulse scrams it. A meltdown takes the fissure and the land.
Turn the collar. Switch on stabilisers round it, evenly.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wiring.button: No launch button: a signal only repeats a set course.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wiring.check: Open the console: every line ticked but the last.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wiring.signal: Give the drive a redstone pulse. A lever will do.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wiring.split: Choose at the table. Launch with redstone. Diagnose at the drive.
aerowarptics.guide.page.wiring.title: Three Jobs, Three Places
aerowarptics.item.rift_pearl.tooltip: 250 mB of Rift Essence in a shell. Thrown, it teleports whatever it hits a short way, like a chorus fruit
aerowarptics.item.scar_chart.none: No uncharted rift scar within reach of here
aerowarptics.item.scar_chart.tooltip: Open it to chart the nearest rift scar nobody has charted yet
aerowarptics.item.ship_compass.unbound: Sneak and use it on a Rift Drive to point it at that ship
aerowarptics.item.stormglass.reading.cle: Clear: no storm within a day
aerowarptics.item.stormglass.reading.gat: Gathering: a storm is due within a day
aerowarptics.item.stormglass.reading.sti: Still: no storm will come on its own
aerowarptics.item.stormglass.tooltip: Use to break it and call a Rift Storm down on the whole server
aerowarptics.item.unset_stormglass.setti: Setting... %1$s seconds out in the storm
aerowarptics.item.unset_stormglass.toolt: Sets only under open sky in a Rift Storm - held, or left on the ground
aerowarptics.jei.info.astrolabe: Laid flat in a square, these form a Cartography Table. One block on its own is already a working table; two by two and three by three chart progressively more ground, and a smaller table is absorbed when you build a bigger one around it. Right-click the finished table for a chart of every anchor within reach, drawn over a survey of the ground around it. It can ride aboard the ship.
aerowarptics.jei.info.berth: Marks out a slip at a Warp Anchor's station. Place it within reach of an anchor you own, then set the slip's size and facing. A ship that warps to that anchor is given the smallest free berth it fits, turned to the berth's facing, and held there: kept still and kept loaded. A ship flown in slowly by hand is caught the same way. If no berth is free, or none is big enough, the warp is refused before it starts. Start the ship's drive to cast off. A comparator reads 15 while a ship is moored.
aerowarptics.jei.info.collapse_cradle: An old machine, rebuilt: three blocks across and three high, placed whole and centred where you aim. Right-click it for its panel. It does two kinds of work, depending on what is in its arms. A stack in its arms, with its folding ingredient in the cup, is folded for Rift Essence, up to sixteen at once. A Rift Core in its arms, a Scar Heart in its cup and offerings on Create Depots around it make a collapse: turn it at a Singularity drive's speed, pipe in essence and start it. Switched-on Spatial Stabilisers around it steady a collapse, as long as they are evenly spaced and not all on one side. If the collapse is unsteady, the machine shakes, sparks and smokes, flings its core clear, and hurts whoever stands too close. If it is very unsteady, it spits the core and offerings back out and keeps only the Scar Heart and the essence. Pipes and funnels connect to any block of its bottom layer. A shaft turns it through the middle of any side of that layer or from under its middle, and no rotation passes through the machine. Start it from the panel or with a redstone pulse on any side. Building one requires a Relic Armillary, which can only be found.
aerowarptics.jei.info.cooling_vent: Placed against a Rift Drive and turned by a shaft, it halves the time the drive takes to cool down after a warp, and blows the heat out as steam when the ship arrives. Up to four coolers count on one drive, and each vent halves what the last one left. Its louvres face away from whatever you place it on and the shaft goes in at the back, so one set straight onto a turning drive is turned by it. A block of ice against the drive works too, with no shaft at all, but only takes a tenth off.
aerowarptics.jei.info.drive_extender: Build a complete cube of these, from two to seven blocks along an edge, with a Rift Drive anywhere inside it. The finished drive is drawn the size of the cube, and every extender in it counts as part of the drive: a shaft against any face of the cube turns it, a Rift Modulator or Spatial Stabiliser placed against any face works as if it were beside the drive, and right-clicking any block opens the drive's console. It does not fly any further for being bigger. Until the cube is complete, extenders do nothing at all, not even carry rotation.
aerowarptics.jei.info.folded_warp_crysta: A Warp Crystal folded at a Collapse Cradle, for Rift Essence. The Mk III is built from it, so the third drive needs a cradle - and so a Relic Armillary from the ruins.
aerowarptics.jei.info.handbook: Every machine in this mod, in the order you would build them. Right-click to open it; the ribbons along the top are the chapters.
aerowarptics.jei.info.opened_rift_lens: A Rift Lens that has been through a rift. Blow a Rift Lens through an open rift with an Encased Fan: a Rift Fissure, a lit Rift Brazier, or an open Rift Gate's pane. Every machine that opens its own rift is built with one, from the Mk II drive up.
aerowarptics.jei.info.relic_armillary: Three bronze rings, one inside the next: the heart of a Collapse Cradle, and the one part of it that nobody knows how to make. It can only be found, never crafted, in barrels in the ruins around rift scars, though not in every one. A Scar Chart leads to the nearest scar nobody has charted.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_beacon: Bind a Rift Beacon by sneaking and right-clicking the Rift Drive of a ship you are standing on. After that, aim at anywhere within sight and right-click, and that ship warps there - you do not have to be aboard it, or anywhere near it. Permission is checked when you bind, so a bound beacon acts as a key: whoever holds it can call the ship. The warp still needs everything an ordinary warp needs: rotation, charge, range, and somewhere the hull fits.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_bond: For a ship built in several sections that only fly alongside each other. Place one on every section, all tuned alike, and a warp takes every section through the rift, sized and checked for room as one ship. Click a placed bond with more in hand to tune them to it. It is not a joint: it holds nothing together in ordinary flight.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_brazier: Burns with rift fire while it has a redstone signal and essence, and rift fire counts as an open rift. Blow items through it with an Encased Fan to rift them, the same way you would wash them. Burns two millibuckets of Rift Essence a second while lit, whether or not anything is passing through.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_casing: A Brass Casing with Warp Dust worked into it - by hand, or by a Deployer. Every machine in this mod that used to take a Brass Casing is built from one.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_chute: Pairs with another Rift Chute anywhere in the world, including one bolted to an airship. Items travel both ways along the pair. Fit a Create funnel to any face to fill it: a chute is an inventory, not a belt attachment. Whichever end sends pays the Rift Essence, charged per item, so a receiving chute needs no supply of its own. A full far end, an unloaded chunk or a ship mid-warp all make items wait in the chute instead of being lost.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_collar: The master block of a Rift Wellhead, which farms Rift Essence from a Rift Fissure you have found. Build a hollow cube round the fissure, with the fissure in its exact middle: Rift Casing for every edge and corner, Warp Glass for every face. The cube is three, five or seven blocks along an edge. Set the collar in the middle of one side, facing out, and put a crystal in it: a Warp Crystal for the small frame, a Folded one for the medium, a Pearlescent one for the large. When the frame is right it forms; if it does not, goggles say what is wrong and where. Feed blocks in through the middle of the top and pipe essence out of the middle of any other face. Turn the collar with a shaft and switch on Spatial Stabilisers around it, evenly spaced, to hold the strain down. A well under more strain digests faster, and strains itself further: past a point it runs away. A comparator reads the strain, and 15 means critical. A redstone pulse, or the panel, scrams it: what it was digesting is lost and the hatch shuts for a while. If the strain reaches the top it melts down. The fissure is destroyed and leaves no Scar Heart, the ground around it is taken, and what is left stays dangerous for some time. A fissure in a wellhead does no rifting and gives nothing to a Spatial Siphon.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_core: The machinery every Rift Drive is built around.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_coupler: Bolted beside a Rift Drive, a Rift Coupler lets several ships warp together as a flotilla. Set one ship's coupler to Flagship and the others to Escort, then take station from each escort's screen: pick a flagship within reach, and its owner accepts (your own ships join without asking). On the flagship's Fleet Board, drag each escort's marker to give it a slot, then press Sound Stations. An escort that holds its slot with a full, turning drive harmonises with the flagship after a few seconds - listen for the hums settling into one note. When every row is ready, press Fold: every ship spins up, counts down, and follows the flagship through the rift, coming out in its slot. Hold Fold instead to go without the ships that are not ready; they are dropped from the flotilla. An escort that drifts out of its slot during the countdown is shaken loose and comes out a few seconds late, off to one side. Set Rift to One on the Fleet Board and the flagship opens one large rift for the whole flotilla instead, which flies in together, in formation, and comes out of one rift at the far end. Every drive still needs its own power and pays its own charge, and a flotilla costs more than the same ships flying alone. The flagship's coupler uses a little Rift Essence per escort during a fold. How many escorts a flagship may lead depends on its drive: one for a Mk I, two for a Mk II, four for a Mk III, and eight for a Singularity. A Display Link reads the coupler's flotilla, or its whole roster, one ship to a line.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_drive: Built into an airship, a Rift Drive folds the whole hull to a Warp Anchor. Rotational force charges it; a jump spends a share of that charge, and costs more for distance and for weight. A drive standing on the ground has nothing to move.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_essence: What a rift sheds when a hull is folded through it. Caught by a Spatial Siphon aboard the ship, and spent dialling Rift Gates.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_gate: The one block of a Rift Gate that does the thinking. It counts as frame, so it can sit anywhere in the ring. Rift Essence pays to dial and to keep the doorway open, and rotational force holds it open - both only at the gate that dialled. If the tank runs dry or the shaft stalls, the gate disconnects. A second gate is needed in the same world to connect to. Run straight Create track into the bottom of its opening and trains go through to the gate it is routed to - set on its dial - waiting at a shut gate while it dials for them.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_gate_frame: Builds the ring of a Rift Gate: standing upright, closed, and enclosing an empty opening of between four and two hundred and twenty-five blocks. That opening is the size limit for anything travelling through.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_goggles: Create's goggles with a rift-ground lens. They read machines exactly as the engineer's goggles do, and they also show Rift Fissures: rifts in the world that are invisible to anyone not wearing them.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_lens: Focuses a rift. Used by every machine here that has to aim one.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_modulator: Bolted beside a Rift Drive, a Rift Modulator lets its pilot choose the colour and theme of the rift the drive opens: the opening, the corridor, the exit shockwave, and even how the rift opens in the first place. Right-click for sixteen colours (left-click sets the core, right-click sets the rim) and a button that cycles through fifteen themes; shift-click the button to cycle backwards. Eight of the themes are nods to warp effects from other works, one is a portal you have almost certainly built, and one is drawn in pencil. Those eight and the Ender theme use their own colours instead of your swatch - hyperspace is blue and white whatever you pick - so the swatches are greyed out while one is chosen. Sketch keeps its paper and pencil look but is coloured in with your swatch. It uses a trickle of Rift Essence only while the linked drive is warping. If the tank runs dry, or the drive is removed, the rift goes back to the drive's own tier colours. A Display Link pointed at the Modulator reads the drive it is linked to, with the same eight readouts the drive itself offers.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_pearl: 250 mB of Rift Essence in an ender pearl's shell, filled by a Spout. It is Rift Essence in item form, for recipes that cannot take a fluid. An Item Drain gets 200 mB back. Thrown, it teleports whatever mob or player it hits to somewhere within eight blocks, like eating a Chorus Fruit. It never affects bosses or anything aboard a ship.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_plotter: The Collapse Cradle's sibling: a field generator three blocks across and three high, placed whole. A dish on a turntable faces the rift it holds, with an armillary ball spinning at its focus. It opens a rift beside itself and another around a target anywhere in the same world, for shipping or for war. Right-click it for its table: type the target's X and Z and press Survey, and the ground there appears as a model you can turn. Set the exit around the target: how far out, which way, how high, and how fast things leave it (their own speed, a set speed, or at rest). Open the Entry tab and the camera moves out beside the machine so you can set where the entry is, how wide, and - on the Face tab - which way it faces, with a hologram of it standing in the world. The Dock and Fire tabs set how it fires: a dock helper lines up a ship waiting behind the entry and launches it through, as far out and as far back as you set it to catch, and an outline in the air shows pilots where to wait; it can fire when a ship docks, on redstone, or hold the rift open as a lane that costs essence each second. It draws Rift Essence as it charges - there is no range limit, a distant target simply costs more - and must be turned at 64 RPM or more. Pipes connect to any block of its bottom layer. A shaft turns it through the middle of any side of that layer or from under its middle, and no rotation passes through the machine. Airships go through with their crew. Unless the server says otherwise, so do players, creatures, shells and TNT. A ship wider than the rift is turned back. Crouch aboard a docked ship to break free. The far rift stays shut until something is on its way through, then opens just before it arrives. Building one requires a Relic Armillary, which can only be found.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_probe: Scans a direction and distance for ground nobody has stood on, and brings back the same map the Astrolabe draws of an anchor. It is the only way to reach somewhere unexplored. Rift Essence pays for each scan; a Rift Drive on the same ship flies the course it finds.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_sunderer: Tears a Rift Fissure open where you want one, and is used up doing it. Build a closed ring of Rift Gate Frame standing on end, as for a Rift Gate, with an opening between 3 by 3 and 7 by 7, and set the Sunderer in the ring where a gate's controller would go, facing out. Fill it with 4 buckets of Rift Essence, turn its shaft at 128 RPM or more, and give it a redstone signal. A point opens in the ring and searches for a far side. It finds none, and becomes a black seed that bends the world around it. A third of the frame lifts out, orbits the seed and is swallowed. Then the seed implodes: the Sunderer is gone, and a fissure hangs in the middle of what is left, seen by everyone for a moment. Keep it turning and keep the ring whole. Stopped while it is still reaching, it misfires: the frame drops back into place and half the essence is handed back. Stopped for long, or broken, once it is straining, it ruptures: the ring, the essence and the ground around it are lost, and nothing is torn. Don't stand in the opening. A torn fissure holds a little essence and gives none to a Spatial Siphon, and seals with no Scar Heart. Unless a Rift Wellhead is built round it within 20 minutes, it gutters shut. It won't fire aboard a ship, in unsettled ground, within 48 blocks of another fissure, near a Warp Anchor or inside a Rift Ward's field.
aerowarptics.jei.info.rift_ward: The third relic: a cracked stone totem bound in a roofless machine, three blocks across and three high, placed whole. It holds a field over the ground round it. A rift aimed into that field - a ship's arrival, a Rift Plotter's far end - comes out at the field's edge instead, and a scan of the ground under it comes back as interference. Its panel sets whom it turns: everyone, everyone but the networks you name, or only the networks you name. You are let through your own unless you tick Turn me too. Turn it at 32 RPM or more, with a shaft into the middle of any side of its bottom layer or from under its middle, and pipe in Rift Essence: it banks a charge, pays a little all the time for the field and a lot for each rift it turns, and its field drops when the charge runs out. While the field stands the totem's pieces hang apart, turn and glow, and the machine hums and gives off light. A Rift Storm thins the field, and a better drive is turned less far out. A comparator reads its charge; it gives a redstone pulse when it turns something aside.
aerowarptics.jei.info.scar_chart: Open it to turn it into a map to the nearest rift scar nobody has charted. A second chart leads somewhere else.
aerowarptics.jei.info.scar_heart: What a Rift Fissure leaves behind when it is emptied and seals. It can only be found, never crafted. A Singularity Core can only be collapsed using one.
aerowarptics.jei.info.scarred_stone: What a Rift Wellhead's meltdown leaves of the ground it did not take. It does nothing. It is only found around a crater.
aerowarptics.jei.info.ship_compass: A compass folded at a Collapse Cradle. It comes out unbound: sneak and use it on a Rift Drive to point it at that ship from then on, loaded or not. It can be bound again the same way. A cross-dimension warp rebuilds the ship, and the compass keeps pointing at where the ship was.
aerowarptics.jei.info.singularity_core: A core collapsed in on itself. Only the Singularity drive is built on one.
aerowarptics.jei.info.spatial_siphon: Carried aboard an airship, a siphon catches the Rift Essence that a completed warp sheds. Longer jumps give more, and every siphon aboard rolls for its own share. Holds four buckets, and pipes can draw the essence off.
aerowarptics.jei.info.spatial_stabiliser: Placed beside a Rift Drive on an airship, it softens sudden changes in the ship's motion while it has a redstone signal - light the burners and the ship eases upward instead of leaping. It stands by while the drive warps, and more than one aboard does not make it stronger.
aerowarptics.jei.info.spatial_wave_detec: Gives off a redstone pulse whenever something arrives through a rift nearby - a ship finishing a warp, or a player, mob or vehicle coming out of a Rift Gate. The closer the arrival, the stronger the signal, from 15 right beside it down to 1 at the edge of its range. Set the range by scrolling on the box on any side, with or without a wrench. It works aboard a ship too.
aerowarptics.jei.info.stabiliser_ring: Holds a warp corridor open while a hull is still inside it.
aerowarptics.jei.info.stormglass: Made by a storm, it knows storms. Its crystals show one of four readings: clear, gathering (a storm within a day), raging, or still (none will come on its own). Break it to call a Rift Storm. This is refused while a storm rages, while the weather is frozen, too soon after the last storm, or where storms are turned off.
aerowarptics.jei.info.unset_stormglass: A glass bottle filled with 500 mB of Rift Essence by a Spout. It only sets under open sky in a Rift Storm. It takes half a minute, either held by a player standing out in the storm or lying on the ground.
aerowarptics.jei.info.warp_anchor: Marks a place an airship can be sent. Right-click to name it and to choose who may travel there: everybody, only you, or the players in a network you put it on. The world keeps the record rather than the block, so an anchor stays a valid destination while its chunks are unloaded. Leave room for the arriving hull.
aerowarptics.jei.info.warp_glass: Glass blown through an open rift with an Encased Fan. A building block that drops itself when broken.

aerowarptics.pack.classic_recipes.title: AeroWarptics: Classic Recipes
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_1: Astrolabe blocks are laid flat, in a square up to three by three
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_2: Complete the square and the table forms itself
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_3: Right-click for the chart: every anchor within reach, drawn over a survey of the ground around it
aerowarptics.ponder.astrolabe.text_4: A table can ride aboard the ship, so a course can be set without landing first
aerowarptics.ponder.collapse_cradle.head: The Collapse
aerowarptics.ponder.collapse_cradle.text: A Collapse Cradle collapses a Singularity Core out of a Rift Core and a Scar Heart
Steady, the core settles back into the arms. Unsteady, it is flung clear. Very unsteady, it spits the core and offerings back out
The collapse knocks back everything near it, and an unsteady one hurts whoever stands too close
However it ends, only the Scar Heart and the essence are used up
It is an old machine, rebuilt: three blocks each way, set down whole where you aim, and too heavy to move
Its rings, the Relic Armillary, can only be found: look in the barrels in rift scar ruins
The Scar Heart comes only from a sealed Rift Fissure. Without one, the core has nothing to collapse into
The offerings stand on Create Depots round it. A Mechanical Arm can load them
Pipe Rift Essence into its bottom layer, and turn it with a shaft into the middle of any side of its floor or up under its middle, at a Singularity drive's own speed
Switched-on Spatial Stabilisers steady the collapse. Space them evenly: a lopsided cage wobbles
A redstone pulse at any side begins it. Anything missing refuses it, before anything is spent
The arms lift the core into the rings, the iris opens and the rift folds into a hole. Stand back: it drags loose objects in as it winds up
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_1: After every warp a Rift Drive has to cool down before it can charge for the next
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_2: A Cooling Vent shortens that. It goes against any face of the drive, with its louvres facing away and its shaft at the back
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_3: Set straight onto a drive that is turning, it is turned by the drive. Turn it with a wrench to feed it from a slower shaft of its own instead
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_4: When a warp completes, a turning vent halves the cooldown and blows the heat out as steam
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_5: Each further vent halves what the last one left
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_6: A block of ice against the drive cools it too, with no shaft at all, but it only takes a tenth off
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_7: Four coolers count on one drive, vents before ice. Any more do nothing, and the goggles show which
aerowarptics.ponder.cooling_vent.text_8: The cooldown is set as the ship arrives, by whatever is cooling the drive at that moment. A vent that has stopped turning by then does not count
aerowarptics.ponder.cradle_folding.text_: A Collapse Cradle can also fold items: it is simpler than a collapse and takes a few seconds
Put a stack of up to sixteen in its arms. The folding ingredient, such as a Shulker Shell, goes in its cup
Every craft uses Rift Essence from its tank, and the shaft has to be turning
Press Begin on its panel, or give it a redstone pulse. The arms lift the stack up to a small rift, which folds it
The result comes back down into the arms, and waits in the tray for you or a funnel to collect it
A Warp Crystal folds into a Folded Warp Crystal. That plus a Shulker Shell folds into a Pearlescent Warp Crystal. A Compass folds into a Ship's Compass
A Ship's Compass comes out unbound. Sneak and use it on a Rift Drive to bind it to that ship
aerowarptics.ponder.drive_extender.text_: A Rift Drive works on its own. Drive Extenders are an optional upgrade, never a requirement
Build a complete cube of them, from two blocks along an edge up to seven, with the drive anywhere inside it - buried in the middle included
Until the cube is finished, the extenders are inert casing. An incomplete frame does nothing and carries nothing
Place the last block and the drive forms. What stands there is now one machine, drawn the size of its frame
A shaft against any face of the cube turns it. Every extender passes the rotation through, so nothing needs to reach the drive itself
Every block of the frame acts as the drive: right-click any of them for the console, and a module against any face links to it
It does not fly any further for being bigger. What a larger frame gives you is room and faces to attach things to, not range
Remove one block and the cube is no longer complete. The frame stops working, and the drive goes back to being a single block
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_1: A Rift Beacon calls a ship you are not standing on, which a normal course cannot do
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_2: Sneak and right-click a Rift Drive to bind the beacon to it. A plain click would only open the console
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_3: Permission is checked here. A beacon cannot be bound to a ship you could not have commanded by hand
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_4: Then aim at anywhere within sight and right-click. The ship is called to whatever the crosshair is on
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_5: The drive still has to be ready: turning fast enough, charged, in range, and with room for the hull to arrive
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_6: If the warp is refused, the beacon says which of these failed, in the same words the drive's own console uses
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_beacon.text_7: If the drive is taken apart, the beacon points at nothing. Bind it again to whatever you build next
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_brazier.text_1: A Rift Brazier burns with rift fire while it has a redstone signal and essence
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_brazier.text_2: Give it a redstone signal. Lit, it burns two millibuckets of Rift Essence a second, whatever is passing
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_brazier.text_3: Blow items through it with an Encased Fan, the same way you would wash them
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_brazier.text_4: A Rift Lens comes out as an Opened Rift Lens. Every drive from the Mk II up is built with them
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_brazier.text_5: Any open rift will do: a Rift Fissure is free for as long as it stays open, and so is an open Rift Gate's pane
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_1: A Rift Chute hands items to another chute, however far apart they are - including one bolted to an airship
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_2: Fit a funnel to any face and feed it from a belt. A chute is an inventory, so it does not sit directly on the belt
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_3: Right-click a chute to name it and pair it with another. Items travel both ways along a pair
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_4: Whichever end sends pays the Rift Essence, per item and only when one crosses. A receiving chute needs no essence of its own
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_chute.text_5: Nothing is ever lost. A full far end, an unloaded chunk or a ship mid-warp all make items wait in the chute instead
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_coupler.text_1: A Rift Coupler fitted to any face of a Rift Drive lets its ship warp together with others, as a flotilla
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_coupler.text_2: Right-click to set its role. One ship is the Flagship: its drive holds the course and commits the jump
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_coupler.text_3: The others are Escorts. At an escort's coupler, take station with a flagship within reach: its owner accepts, and your own ships join straight away
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_coupler.text_4: On the flagship's Fleet Board, drag each escort to a slot, then press Sound Stations. Every ship in the flotilla hears the horn
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_coupler.text_5: An escort holding its slot with a full, turning drive harmonises with the flagship. Listen for the hums settling on one note
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_coupler.text_6: Every drive still needs its own power and pays its own charge, and a fleet costs more than the same ships flying alone
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_coupler.text_7: When every escort is ready, press Fold. A ship that drifts out of its slot during the countdown is shaken loose, and arrives late and off to one side
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_1: A Rift Drive moves an entire airship to a Warp Anchor, hull and cargo and crew together
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_2: It has to be built into the ship. A drive standing on the ground has nothing to move
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_3: Rotational force spins it up. Below the drive's minimum speed it will not charge at all
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_4: Charge builds while it turns. A jump spends a share of it - more for distance, more for a heavy ship
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_5: Right-click for the console: pick an anchor, and the drive quotes the cost before committing
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_drive.text_6: Mk I to Singularity buy reach, speed and efficiency. The Singularity pays for its range with an unsteady arrival
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_1: Ruins generate where someone's gate went wrong: a broken ring, a sunken vault, a survey mast
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_2: A Rift Fissure hangs in the middle of one. It is a rift that never closed, still leaking Rift Essence
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_3: It is invisible. It has no model and no outline, and you cannot bump into it - you could stand in the ruin and never know
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_4: Wear Rift Infused Goggles. Only then is the fissure drawn, and only then can you aim at it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_5: They are Create's goggles with a rift-ground lens, so they read every machine that the engineer's goggles do
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure.text_6: A fissure cannot be broken. The only way to get rid of one is to empty it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_fissure_closing: The fissure stands here, visible only through the goggles
Stand a Spatial Siphon within a few blocks of it. Nothing else is needed: no shaft, no redstone
The fissure hands over its essence steadily, and shrinks as it empties
A fissure holds several times what a single siphon does, so pipe the essence away or stand more than one siphon nearby
More siphons do not fill any faster. The fissure's own rate is the limit, not the plumbing
Once empty, it seals for good. It cannot be brought back
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_1: Rift Gate Frame builds a ring standing upright, enclosing an empty opening
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_2: The opening is the size limit. Whatever fits through it can travel - and nothing larger can
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_3: Anything from four blocks of opening up to two hundred and twenty-five will form
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_4: One block of the ring is a Rift Gate controller. It counts as frame, so it may sit anywhere in the circle
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate.text_5: A second gate has to be built somewhere else in the same world. A gate on its own connects to nothing
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_gate_dialling.t: Rotational force holds the gate's opening open. If the speed drops, the gate disconnects
A wider opening is harder to hold and costs more to dial
Rift Essence pays to dial, and keeps being used every second the doorway stays open
Right-click the controller and choose which gate to connect to
Only the dialling gate pays. The far end needs no rotation and no essence of its own
Walk in, or drive in. A vehicle leaves the far gate in the direction that gate faces, keeping its speed
Both ends must lie in the same world. A gate cannot reach into another dimension
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_modulator.text_: A Rift Modulator bolted beside a Rift Drive lets its pilot choose the colour of the rift it opens, and even how the rift opens
It reads whichever drive it touches, and takes its facing from that drive when it is placed
It uses a trickle of Rift Essence, and only while the drive is warping. An idle drive costs it nothing
Right-click for a choice of colours (left-click sets the core, right-click sets the rim), a matching theme, and a slider for how strong the effect is
If it runs out of essence or is removed, the rift goes back to the drive's own tier colours
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_1: Every other destination is somewhere a player has placed an anchor. A Rift Probe is how you reach ground nobody has visited
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_2: Right-click it, pick a direction on the dial and a distance on the slider, then scan ahead
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_3: Rift Essence pays for each scan, and scanning further costs more. A Spatial Siphon is how you collect it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_4: The wait is the world being generated. A scan aimed at unexplored ground has to generate that ground before it can map it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_5: What comes back is the same chart the Astrolabe draws for an anchor, so a blind jump is judged on the same evidence as any other
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_probe.text_6: Send the ship there and the Rift Drive flies it. There is no anchor at the far end yet, so bring one if you want to return
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_sunderer.text_1: Build a closed ring of Rift Gate Frame standing on end, as for a Rift Gate. The opening may be three to seven blocks across
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_sunderer.text_2: Set a Rift Sunderer in the ring where a gate's controller would go, facing out. Its one shaft is on its back
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_sunderer.text_3: Fill it with four buckets of Rift Essence and turn it at 128 RPM or more. It lights as it fills
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_sunderer.text_4: A redstone signal fires it. A point searches the ring for a far side and finds none. A third of the frame lifts out and orbits a black seed, and is swallowed. Keep it turning and stand clear
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_sunderer.text_5: The seed implodes. The Sunderer is used up, and a Rift Fissure hangs where the opening was. Everyone sees it born; after that, only Rift Goggles show it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_sunderer.text_6: A torn fissure gives a siphon nothing and seals with no Scar Heart. Build a Rift Wellhead round it within twenty minutes or it gutters shut
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_sunderer.text_7: Stopped while it is still reaching, it misfires and gives half the essence back. Stopped later, or broken, it ruptures and takes the ground
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_wellhead.text_1: Build a hollow cube round a Rift Fissure, with the fissure in its exact middle: Rift Casing for the edges, Warp Glass for the faces
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_wellhead.text_2: Set a Rift Collar in the middle of one side and put a Warp Crystal in it. A five or seven block frame needs a better crystal
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_wellhead.text_3: Feed blocks in through the middle of the top. Rougher blocks strain the fissure more
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_wellhead.text_4: Pipe Rift Essence out of the middle of any other face
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_wellhead.text_5: Turn the collar with a shaft, and switch on Spatial Stabilisers round it, evenly spaced, to hold the strain down
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_wellhead.text_6: More strain digests faster, and strains it further. A comparator reads it, and a redstone pulse scrams it
aerowarptics.ponder.rift_wellhead.text_7: Let the strain reach the top and it melts down: the fissure, the frame and the ground round them are gone
aerowarptics.ponder.spatial_siphon.text_: A Spatial Siphon is built into an airship, not onto the ground
Passing a hull through folded space sheds some Rift Essence. The siphons aboard catch it
One catch per jump, shared between every siphon aboard. More siphons hold more, but do not catch more. Longer jumps give more
Four buckets fit inside. Pipes can draw the essence off into storage
Rift Essence is what dials a Rift Gate
aerowarptics.ponder.spatial_stabiliser.t: A Spatial Stabiliser is a Rift Drive module. It goes against any face of a drive that is built into an airship
It has no screen and nothing to set. A redstone signal switches it on, and losing the signal switches it off
Left alone, a hull does what its machinery tells it, as fast as the physics allows. Light the burners under a balloon and the ship leaps upward
Switched on, it cancels most of each tick's change in motion. The same push now eases the ship upward instead
The ship still goes wherever it is pushed. It just responds as though it were several times heavier
A blow too hard to come from machinery, such as a hillside or a hard landing, passes through untouched, so the ship is never cushioned into the ground it just hit
While its drive is flying a warp, it stands by. The flight was planned in full before the rift opened, and resisting it would only drag the ship off course
A second stabiliser aboard makes no difference. One holds the ship and the rest stand by. The goggles show which is which
aerowarptics.ponder.spatial_wave_detecto: A Spatial Wave Detector listens for anything arriving through a rift nearby
Scroll on the box on any side to set how far it listens. The server may cap how far that can be
When a ship finishes a warp, or anyone steps out of a Rift Gate within range, it gives off a pulse of redstone
The closer the arrival, the stronger the signal. Right beside it gives 15, and the very edge of its range gives 1
A ship is measured from its nearest part, not its middle. If a long hull's bow comes out beside the detector, the ship counts as arriving beside it
It only hears arrivals, never departures. Another arrival during a pulse restarts the pulse
It works aboard an airship too, and hears its own ship arrive at full strength
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_1: A Warp Anchor is somewhere an airship can be sent
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_2: Right-click it to give it a name, and to say whether other players may travel to it
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_3: The world keeps the record, not the block. An anchor stays a valid destination even while its chunks are unloaded
aerowarptics.ponder.warp_anchor.text_4: Leave room around it. An arriving hull has to fit, and the drive will refuse an anchor whose space is blocked
aerowarptics.recipe.agitating.clean: Clean feed: strains the tear least
aerowarptics.recipe.agitating.essence: Digests to %1$s mB of Rift Essence
aerowarptics.recipe.agitating.fair: Fair feed: strains the tear less
aerowarptics.recipe.agitating.rough: Rough feed: strains the tear hard
aerowarptics.recipe.collapse.stake: If it goes wrong, only the Scar Heart is lost
aerowarptics.recipe.collapse.time: About %1$s seconds, less in a Rift Storm
aerowarptics.recipe.folding.essence: %1$s mB of Rift Essence a craft
aerowarptics.recipe.folding.stack: Up to sixteen fold at once
aerowarptics.recipe.rifting.fan: Encased Fan through an open rift
aerowarptics.rift_plotter.aboard: Too heavy for any hull: set it down on the ground
aerowarptics.rift_plotter.no_room: Needs clear room three blocks across and three high, centred where you aim
aerowarptics.rift_ward.aboard: Too heavy for any hull: set it down on the ground
aerowarptics.rift_ward.no_room: Needs clear room three blocks across and three high, centred where you aim
aerowarptics.stormglass.call.called: The glass shatters, and the sky begins to tear open
aerowarptics.stormglass.call.forbidden: The glass will not break - storms cannot be called here
aerowarptics.stormglass.call.frozen: The weather is frozen; a storm called now would never end
aerowarptics.stormglass.call.too_soon: Too soon after the last storm - the glass holds
aerowarptics.sunderer.failure.aboard_shi: Can't tear a fissure aboard a ship
